title: PRA credentials, credential pools and the credentials policy

prose.text: Credentials decide who logs in to a console, and pools let several users share them.

checks.do: Whether the credential type matches the console protocol, since type cannot change after creation.
Whether a failed session start is a pool whose credentials are all in use, before looking at policy or approval.
Whether a credentials policy still assigns the credential or pool to the console.
Whether the policy that should inject a credential is the last privileged credentials policy, which the page says is not applied, or whether fewer than two policies exist.
Whether a pool-sizing or rotation answer rests on the unverified release-at-session-end statement.

credential-types.statement: Privileged credentials come in three types: Username+Password for RDP with an optional domain, SSH Key with a username, private key and optional passphrase, and Password for VNC or RealVNC.

quotes: Credential Type: Select one of the following options:
Username+Password: Select if you are using an RDP protocol.
SSH Key: Select if you are using an SSH protocol.
Password: Select if you are using a VNC or RealVNC protocol.
Domain: (Optional) Enter the domain name associated with the username.
SSH Key: Enter the SSH private key associated with the username for the login you want to use for the privileged credential.
Passphrase: (Optional) Enter the password that is used to protect the SSH private key.
Username: Enter the username for the login you want to use for the privileged credential.
evidence.after: SSH Key: Select if you are using an SSH protocol.

domain-only-for-ad-rdp.statement: The domain needs to be specified only when logging in to an RDP console connected to an Active Directory domain; it can also be included in the username.

quotes: The domain name only needs to be specified when logging in to an RDP console that is connected to an Active Directory domain.
You can also include the domain name as part of the username.

ssh-key-size.statement: SSH private keys of 2048 bits or smaller can be used for a privileged credential.

quotes: You can only use SSH private keys that are 2048-bit length or smaller.

type-immutable.statement: A credential's type cannot be changed after it is created and saved; Username+Password is the type for RDP and SSH Key the type for SSH.

quotes: You cannot change the Credential Type after it's been created and saved.
Username+Password: Select if you are using an RDP protocol.
SSH Key: Select if you are using an SSH protocol.
You cannot change the Credential Type setting.

rdp-credential-not-for-ssh.statement: A credential made for RDP therefore cannot be switched to serve SSH.
rdp-credential-not-for-ssh.conditions: Follows from type-immutable: the type is fixed once saved, and the help ties Username+Password to RDP and SSH Key to SSH. No source states that a credential cannot serve a protocol other than its type's, or what Private Access does when a credential of one type is used for a console of another protocol.

pool-purpose.statement: A credential pool maps authentication details to a privileged console through a privileged credentials policy that uses SAML and SCIM criteria, so multiple users can start sessions without entering credentials.

quotes: After you create a privileged credential pool, you can map it to a privileged console by creating a privileged credential policy using the SAML and SCIM policy criteria types.
Allow users to start a privileged console session without needing to provide credentials.

pool-exhaustion.statement: When all credentials in a pool are exhausted or in use, users are prevented from accessing the privileged console.

quotes: Prevent users from accessing the privileged console if all privileged credentials from the privileged credentials pool are exhausted or in use.

pool-sources.statement: Before using credential pools an admin must discover credentials from external identity sources such as Active Directory or Entra ID, or create them locally, and must have created the portals and consoles the credentials will be assigned to.

quotes: you must first discover credentials from external identity sources (e.g., Active Directory (AD) or Entra ID) or create credentials locally in the Zscaler Admin Console.
You also need to create the privileged portals and privileged consoles that you want to assign the credentials to.

pool-type.statement: A credential pool has a credential type of SSH, RDP, VNC or RealVNC.

quotes: The protocol type that was designated for the privileged credential pool (SSH, RDP, VNC, or RealVNC).

microtenant-inheritance.statement: Privileged credentials created in the Default Microtenant are inherited across microtenants.

quotes: Privileged credentials that are created in the Default Microtenant are inherited across Microtenants.
Privileged credentials that are created in the Default Microtenant are inherited across Microtenants.

credential-injection.statement: Based on the privileged credentials policy, credentials are automatically injected into the privileged console without having to be added manually.

quotes: Based on the privileged credentials policy, credentials are automatically injected into the privileged console without having to manually add them.

credential-prerequisites.statement: To use a privileged credential, a privileged portal and a privileged console must first be created, and they are then assigned to the privileged credential.

quotes: To use a privileged credential, you must first create a privileged portal and a privileged console.
The privileged portal and privileged console are then assigned to the privileged credential.

update-after-change.statement: If the underlying credentials are changed after the privileged credential was created and saved, the new details (for example username, password or private key) must be updated on the privileged credential to continue using it.

quotes: If the credentials are changed after you created and saved the privileged credential, you must update the new credential details (e.g., Username, Password, Private Key) to continue using the privileged credential.

move-needs-policy-removal.statement: From the Managed page a privileged credential can be deleted or moved into a Microtenant; if privileged credential policies are associated with it, those policies must be deleted to move it to a different Microtenant.

quotes: Select to view additional actions, including deleting a privileged credential and moving the privileged credential into a Microtenant.
If privileged credential policies are associated with the privileged credential, then the policies must be deleted to move the privileged credential to a different Microtenant.

pool-type-immutable.statement: A credential pool's Credential Type is a sign-in protocol type: Username+Password for RDP, SSH Key for SSH and Password for VNC or RealVNC. It cannot be changed after the pool is created and saved, and the edit page says the Credential Type field setting cannot be changed.

quotes: Credential Type: Select a sign-in protocol type.
Username+Password: Select if you are using an RDP protocol.
SSH Key: Select if you are using an SSH protocol.
Password: Select if you are using a VNC or RealVNC protocol.
You cannot change the Credential Type after it's been created and saved.
You cannot change the Credential Type field setting.

pool-fields.statement: A credential pool groups and organizes existing privileged credentials: it takes a name (which cannot contain special characters other than periods, hyphens and underscores) and the privileged credentials to group together.

quotes: Name: Enter a name for the privileged credential pool. The name cannot contain special characters, with the exception of periods (.), hyphens (-), and underscores ( _ ).
Privileged Credentials: Select the privileged credentials that you want to group together.
You can create privileged credential pools to group and organize existing privileged credentials.

credentials-policy-assigns.statement: A privileged credentials policy rule assigns either one privileged credential or one credential pool to consoles. When a user opens a console with such a policy they reach it without logging in, and deleting the policy removes the assignment so the console prompts for a login again.

quotes: When an end user accesses a privileged console that has an assigned privileged credentials policy, the end user can access the privileged console without manually logging in.
If you delete the privileged credentials policy, the privileged credentials associated with the privileged consoles for that policy are removed
The credentials prompt the end user to log in, replacing the credential-provided access.
Select if you want to assign a privileged credential or a privileged credential pool of multiple credentials for this policy.

credentials-page.statement: The Privileged Credentials page shows data over 1 hour to 365 days. It counts used privileged credentials that are SSH, RDP, VNC and RealVNC enabled, and per credential pool shows Used Credentials, the amount currently being used from the pool, and Total Credentials, the total within the pool.

quotes: View privileged credential data over a period between 1 hour and 365 days.
SSH: The total number of used privileged credentials that are SSH enabled.
RDP: The total number of used privileged credentials that are RDP enabled.
VNC: The total number of used privileged credentials that are VNC enabled.
RealVNC: The total number of used privileged credentials that are RealVNC enabled.
Used Credentials: The amount of privileged credentials that are currently being used from that privileged credential pool.
Total Credentials: The total amount of privileged credentials within that privileged credential pool.

credentials-policy-limit.statement: A privileged credentials policy allows 5,000 policy rules and 1,000 privileged consoles per policy.

quotes: | Privileged Credentials Policy | 5,000 policy rules 1,000 privileged consoles per privileged credentials policy |

credentials-policy-purpose.statement: A privileged credentials policy rule maps privileged credentials, or privileged credential pools, to the associated privileged console using SAML and SCIM information, so designated consoles have designated credentials. A privileged credential's protocol can be SSH, RDP, RealVNC or VNC with the related login details.

quotes: When you create a privileged credential, you can select the protocol (SSH, RDP, RealVNC, or VNC) and add the related login details (i.e., username, password, SSH key, etc).

After the privileged credential and privileged credential pools are set up, you can create the privileged credentials policy to map the privileged credentials to the associated privileged console using SAML and SCIM information.
Assign privileged consoles to have designated privileged credentials or privileged credential pools to allow users to access them.

credentials-policy-prerequisites.statement: Credentials-based control needs the privileged consoles it will be assigned to created first, then the privileged credential or privileged credential pools the policy will be applied to.

quotes: If you want to configure privileged credentials-based control, you must first create the privileged consoles that you want to assign control to. Then you need to create the privileged credential or privileged credential pools that you're going to apply the policy to.

credentials-policy-last-rule.statement: The Privileged Credentials Policy page says at least two privileged credential policies must be created for the first rule to apply, that the privileged credential of the last policy is not applied to its related console, and that the last policy should be one that is not needed.

quotes: You need to have at least two privileged credential policies created for the first rule privileged credential policy to apply.
The privileged credential associated with the last privileged credential policy won't be applied to its related privileged console.
Ensure that the last privileged credential policy is one that you do not need to use.

credentials-policy-last-rule.conditions: Stated under the Rule Order column; the page does not say whether this is by design or a defect.

credentials-policy-columns.statement: The Privileged Credentials Policy page lists each rule's Rule Order (ZPA applies rules in the listed order and the number can be edited by entering a new value) and its Credential, the privileged credential or credential pool assigned to the rule.

quotes: Rule Order: The policy evaluation order number for the rule. Private Access (ZPA) applies policy rules based on the order they are listed here. Change the rule order by clicking on the number and manually entering a new value.
Credential: The name of the privileged credential or privileged credential pool you have assigned for that specific policy rule.

last-rule-reason.title: Why the last privileged credentials policy is not applied
last-rule-reason.detail: The page states that at least two policies are needed and that the last one's credential is not applied, but not why, or whether a default rule exists. An uncited legacy API capture shows defaultRule and defaultRuleName fields on credential-policy rules (vendor/zscaler-help/legacy-api-configuring-privileged-policies-using-api.json); that was not checked here and may bear on this. A lab test with two policies, or a read of that capture, would resolve it.

pool-return-and-rotation.title: Credential return, queueing and rotation in a pool
pool-return-and-rotation.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "When the session ends, the cred returns to the pool. Cred rotation is a central action - rotate the pool, every user's next session uses the new cred. Pool exhaustion = access block, not queue ... Size pools for peak, not average" and "the DBA never sees the password." The help says access is prevented when all credentials are in use (claim pool-exhaustion) and that users need not provide credentials; it does not say the credential is released at session end, that sessions are never queued, or that rotation propagates. Rotation does exist, per managed credential rather than as a pool action: a credential class schedules it (Scheduled, After Each Use or Never) and a Rotate action does it in real time (zpa.pra.managed-credentials:rotation-policies, zpa.pra.managed-credentials:rotate-now); the pages never describe rotating a pool. Still unstated: whether a pooled credential is released at session end, whether sessions queue, whether After Each Use rotation fires at session end, and whether locally created credentials can rotate. A lab test of a pool with one credential and two sessions would resolve it.
